messages:
sre-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - streaming.decode.p99 > 1200ms across us-west-2. Threshold crossed at 2987654300. Paging observed on worker nodes. :rotating_light:

carmen: seeing large tail spikes for streaming endpoints, p95 ~ 450ms, p99 ~ 1.3s. Error rate still low but lots of stalls. Dash: https://redwood.internal/observability/streams/ingress?id=us-west-2

ashok: confirmed. Patterns coincide with kernel rollout started ~ 2987654000 (trt8 + flashattn-v2 schedule). Lots of decode threads stuck in memcpy/pagelist.

mika: interestingly only on models with sequence > 1024 and streaming enabled. Short requests look fine. Might be KV/cache eviction interaction.

jen: customer-impact check: top-5 customers by QPS show 20% increased tail latency, one customer (acme-inc) reported degraded streaming UX. Not seeing circuit-breaker trips yet.

carmen: bootstrapping live mitigations: 1) route streaming traffic to older kernel pool (rollout rollback), 2) enable fallback to baseline kernel for sequences > 1024, 3) increase cache retention for prefix keys for 10m. Doing 1) now.

deploy-bot: roll request accepted. Rolling back kernel rollout on node group rg-streaming-usw2-kernel-v2 -> v1. Initiating cordon/drain for 6 nodes.

ashok: while rollback runs, add a routing policy to prefer dedicated-capacity pools for affected customers to reduce cross-tenant paging. I'll submit a policy change: `route-policy add prefer:deds for tag:streaming_large_seq`

mika: logs from one affected pod:
```
[decode.cpp:413] KVCache::evict() evict_count=0 free_pages=0
[trt_kernel.cc:89] memcpy_async returned 11 (out of memory?)
[flash_attn.cu:202] tail-latency: blocked on gpu_page_alloc
```
Pointing to compile path change that altered allocator behavior.

jen: SLA monitoring: p95 SLO is 300ms for streaming; currently p95 breach since 2987654285. Need comms if we can't stabilize in 30m.

carmen: rollback progress: 3/6 nodes reverted. Early telemetry shows p99 dropping from 1.3s -> 850ms on those nodes. Still overall high.

ops-infra: I can temporarily increase instance count in the fallback pool to absorb traffic. Will spin 4 more nodes (g4dn.xlarge) and attach to streaming pool. ETA ~ 7m.

mika: we should also flip the compiler flag we shipped with the kernel build: `--enable-async-mem` was introduced in the compilepath. That flag changes the allocator behavior for repeated KV cache touch patterns. Revert recommended.

ashok: can we safely hotpatch the flag without full rollback? Possibly via env override: set RT_ENABLE_ASYNC_MEM=0 on runtime config and restart tasks. Doing a canary on 1 node now.

carmen: canary looks promising: that node's p99 now 480ms. Let's propagate to remaining nodes after verifying no regressions for short sequences.

deploy-bot: env update applied to 1 canary pod. Restarted pod id: pod-stream-ax12.

jen: comms draft: "We're investigating elevated tail latency on streaming endpoints after a kernel/compile change. Some requests may experience stalls up to ~1.3s. We're rolling back the kernel rollout and applying a runtime flag revert to mitigate. We'll update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?

mika: good. Add note re: affected traffic types (long seq, streaming) and ask customers to retry streaming responses if they see stalls.

carmen: metrics after env flip propagation step: p95 -> 310ms, p99 -> 560ms, stalls decreased by ~70% across reverted nodes. Overall still above SLO but trending down.

ashok: follow-ups: 1) full rollback complete ETA 12m, 2) apply RT_ENABLE_ASYNC_MEM=0 across runtime pools, 3) revert kernel release artifacts from CI to block re-deploy, 4) create postmortem ticket and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml for compilepath root cause.

ops-infra: extra nodes spun and absorbing traffic. No increase in OOMs observed.

mika: preliminary root cause hypothesis: change in compilepath optimized memcpy path for flashattn that inadvertently changed page allocation / alignment and interacted poorly with our KV cache eviction heuristic -> led to increased paging during long-sequence streaming. TRTs tight memory paths exacerbated it.

jen: customer impact summary to include in postmortem: start 2987654285, partial mitigations rolled 2987654330, majority of traffic back to baseline by 2987654400. Affected customers: acme-inc (degraded UX), several small PLG users saw elevated tail. No data loss or error-rate increase.

carmen: handing off to night on-call: @mika you own the followup patch verification (test vectors for long seq streaming + KV stress). @ashok please coordinate CI gating to block the problematic kernel/compile flags until we have better alloc tests. Leave this thread pinned.

mika: ack. will run extended load test overnight and post results here.

ashok: ack. will put a temporary block in pipeline and notify release managers.

jen: I'll kick off the postmortem ticket and draft customer comms. If we hold SLO breach for > 1h we'll escalate to customer success for emails.

sre-bot: Handoff note: oncall -> night-sre (mika) at 2987654378. Incident marked mitigated but monitoring for recurrence. Tags: paging, kernel-rollback, streaming-tail, compilepath

carmen: thanks team. Leaving handoff notes in runbook and incident ticket. If anyone sees re-emergence ping this thread. :wave:
